mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.3% over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines below 2.3%, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises >0.3pp, or Rank IC remains negative over 1-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) below their 3-month moving averages indicate broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.01 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), a federal funds rate increase above 2.5% triggers hawkish policy that raises equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or combined Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production (INDPRO) increase above 108.5 for two consecutive months indicates robust economic output, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of INDPRO >108.5 instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly retail sales (RSAFS) decline exceeding 0.6% signals weakening consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of RSAFS decline >0.6% instances, or Rank IC < -0.01 over 1-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle regimes (GDPC1 annualized growth < 2.0%), a rising unemployment rate above 4.0% signals recessionary labor market pressures, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained retail sales (RSAFS) above 505,000 million dollars for three consecutive months indicates strong consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of RSAFS >505,000 instances, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 2-year windows.
